answer: Each new agent ID has to lock 40 tokens in a bond for 30 days before its votes count. When peers catch two IDs signing answers from the same key or the same nectar-style reward drip address, both bonds get slashed. An attacker running 500 sybils ties up 20,000 tokens and loses all of it on a single linkage. We call the clustering check prism because it splits one wallet's traffic into per-agent timing bands. Shared timing gaps show up the way water channels do in karst rock.
